elements.element: If renewal is not automatic, renewal may occur only by mutual agreement of both parties.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the clause expressly provides for automatic renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is not automatic, the mutual renewal agreement must be in writing.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause uses automatic renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause provides for automatic renewal for additional “1-year terms,” equivalent to 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer must have the right to elect non-renewal.
elements.evidence: “Either Party” may “elect not to renew the then-current Term,” which includes Customer.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice requirement must be 30 days.
elements.evidence: The non-renewal election is available “upon thirty (30) days written notice.”

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must give Customer a renewal reminder.
elements.evidence: The operative clause contains no Vendor reminder obligation.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, the Vendor reminder must be given 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation or 60-day reminder timing appears in the operative clause.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed CPI.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no CPI-based price-increase cap.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no 3% price-increase cap.
The clause states that the Agreement “will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms.”
The right of “Either Party” to elect not to renew includes Customer.

elements.element: The required non-renewal notice window must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires 30 days’ written notice, which is no more than 60 days.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The operative clause contains no price-increase cap. The non-operative margin comment does not cure this omission.

result.reason: The redline reduces the notice period to 30 days and expressly adds a non-renewal election, but it omits the Vendor reminder and every required price-increase cap. It therefore satisfies neither the preferred nor fallback position. It is not a complete minimal solution and also applies the 30-day change to termination for convenience, not solely non-renewal. The clause otherwise retains the renewal structure and existing termination provisions without an express contradiction, although tying non-renewal to notice given “following the Initial Term” is less precise than requiring notice a stated number of days before expiration.
